description: Recommends 5-year tax abatement for 410 and 420 5th Avenue North.
Project includes 474 rental units and ground floor commercial.
Total municipal/library abatement estimated at $2.72 million.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
6 for, 0 against
Administration explained setting a start date provides budget certainty for mill rate impacts.
This is the first abatement extension under the new 2023 policy amendments.
The provincial government has not yet approved its portion of the tax abatement.

description: Committee recommends increasing 2025 prepaid servicing rates.
Preliminary 2026 rates would be set at 2025 levels.
Residential, commercial rates would rise by 2.9%.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
6 for, 0 against
City Manager Jorgenson explained Saskatoon's "growth pays for growth" approach.
New residential, commercial, institutional, and industrial developments are affected.
Home Builders Association raised concerns about school levies and high rates.
The legality of school levies is currently a matter before the courts.
Administration will report on underground electrical servicing and levy benchmarking in 2026.

segments.title: Administration introduces prepaid servicing rates report
segments.takeaway: Administration presented the annual report requesting approval for adjusted 2025 and preliminary 2026 prepaid servicing rates, explaining the cost recovery model and proposed increases.

segments.title: Questions on cost competitiveness and benchmarking
segments.takeaway: Committee members questioned administration on measures to ensure competitiveness in construction costs and the challenges of benchmarking Saskatoon's levy rates against other municipalities.

segments.title: Discussion on removing underground electrical servicing from prepaid rates
segments.takeaway: Administration confirmed ongoing discussions with the Home Builders Association regarding the potential removal of underground electrical servicing from prepaid rates.

segments.title: Feasibility of "apples to apples" levy rate comparison
segments.takeaway: Administration discussed the difficulty of an "apples to apples" comparison of levy rates across municipalities due to differing infrastructure delivery and funding models.

segments.title: Questions on school levies
segments.takeaway: Administration confirmed the city's position that legislation allows for school levies, a matter currently before the courts, despite industry concerns.

segments.title: Additional motions for future reporting
segments.takeaway: Committee members moved additional motions requesting future reports on electrical servicing rates and an "apples to apples" comparison of levy rates.

segments.title: Committee approves recommendations and additional motions
segments.takeaway: The committee unanimously approved the original recommendation along with the two additional motions for future reporting.

description: Committee recommends increasing 2025 Parks and Recreation Levy 4.37%.
Elementary School Levy up 13%; High School Levy down 5.6%.
New rates apply to lots serviced after January 1, 2025.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
6 for, 0 against
Mayor Block clarified province discussed contributing a third of future school land costs.
Developers and future property owners in Saskatoon will pay new rates.
Administration will report back in 2026 on new provincial school land act.
